No experience of the terminal, Git or programming is assumed. Keep this page open, and look things up when you need them.

Claude can also explain anything in the workshop. Ask it what a word or an error message means. To set something up, type /workshop-queries and then what you want to do.

Two places to type

You type in two different places, and it matters which one you use.

Terminal Claude
What it is Talks to the computer Talks to the model
What it accepts Commands, exactly as written Plain language and / commands
How it looks A line ending in $ A box with a >
Example git status What does this script do?
On the slides A dark box marked $ A dark box marked ›

Claude runs inside the terminal. While it is open, what you type goes to Claude. To run a terminal command, you have three choices:

  • Type /exit to leave Claude, and claude --continue to return
  • Open a second terminal with the + at the top of the terminal panel
  • Start the line with ! inside Claude, for one command: ! git status

The terminal

The terminal is a text interface to the computer. You type a command, press Enter and read the result. Many commands print nothing when they succeed.

A command has parts:

ls -a papers
Part Name Meaning
ls Command List files
-a Option Include hidden files
papers Argument Which folder
Key Effect
Tab Completes a file or folder name
↑ Brings back the previous command
Ctrl+C Stops the running command
Ctrl+Shift+C (Cmd+C on a Mac) Copies selected text
Ctrl+Shift+V (Cmd+V on a Mac) Pastes

In the terminal, Ctrl+C does not copy. It stops whatever is running.

Nothing appears on screen while you type a password. That is normal.

Files and folders

Term Meaning
Path Where a file is: papers/paper.pdf is paper.pdf in the folder papers
Current folder Where the terminal is now. pwd shows it
~ Your home folder
. The current folder
.. The folder one level up
Hidden file A name starting with ., such as .env. ls -a shows it
Extension The end of a file name, such as .csv, which says what kind of file it is

Git and GitHub

Git records versions of a folder, so you can see what changed and go back. GitHub is a website that keeps a copy of that record. Git runs on your machine, and GitHub is where the copy lives.

Term Meaning
Repository, or repo A folder that Git tracks
Commit One saved version, with a message saying what changed
Push Send your commits to GitHub
Pull Fetch commits from GitHub
Clone Download a repository to a new machine
Branch A separate line of work in a repository. You will use main
Remote, or origin The copy on GitHub
.gitignore A list of files that Git must leave out

The cycle for saving work:

git status
git add -A
git commit -m "Describe what changed"
git push

Ask Claude to do this for you, and read what it shows. For the full steps, including how to undo a mistake:

/workshop-queries how do I save and undo work with Git?

Keys and services

Term Meaning
API A way for a program to ask a service for data
API key, or token A long password that identifies you to a service
.env A text file in your project that holds keys, so they stay out of your code
Rate limit How many requests a service allows in a period

Anyone who has your key can use your account, at your expense. Never paste a key into a conversation with Claude, because the conversation is sent to the model provider. Paste it into .env in the VS Code editor. If a key does reach a conversation or GitHub, delete it with the provider and create a new one.

Installing software

Term Meaning
Package Code that someone else wrote and that your project uses
Environment The set of packages for one project, kept apart from others
uv Installs Python, packages and tools. uvx runs a tool without installing it
Package manager A program that installs software: Homebrew on a Mac, winget on Windows, apt on Linux
PATH The list of folders where the terminal looks for commands. command not found often means a new tool is not on it yet: open a new terminal

Everything is already installed in your workspace. You need these terms only for your own laptop.

Servers and SSH

Term Meaning
Server A computer that runs all the time in a data centre
Workspace Your own computer on the workshop server, used through the browser
SSH A secure way to open a terminal on another computer
Key pair Two files for SSH. The private key stays with you and the public key goes on the server
Root The administrator account on a server
Port A numbered door for a service. SSH uses 22
Firewall Rules that decide which connections reach a server
Tunnel A private connection that makes a port on a server appear on your machine
DNS The records that connect a domain name to a server
Docker Runs a program in a sealed box, with everything it needs

Claude’s vocabulary

Term Meaning
Model The AI that reads text and writes a reply: Opus, Sonnet or Haiku
Token A word or part of a word. Models read, write and charge by the token
Context window Everything the model can see at once
Prompt What you ask
Tool Something Claude can do, such as read a file or run a command
Agent A model that uses tools in a loop until a task is done
Skill Instructions in a file, which Claude loads when they apply
Subagent A helper with its own context that does one job
MCP server A small program or web service that gives Claude extra tools
Plugin A package of skills, subagents and MCP servers

File formats

Format What it is
Markdown (.md) Plain text with simple marks, such as # for a heading
CSV (.csv) A table as plain text
Parquet (.parquet) A compact file for large tables
JSON (.json) Structured text, often for settings
YAML Settings between --- lines at the top of a file
BibTeX (.bib) A list of references for LaTeX

When something goes wrong

Error messages are normal, including for experts. Most say exactly what is wrong.

  1. Read the last lines of the message. The cause is usually there
  2. Copy the message into Claude and ask what it means
  3. If Claude is doing the wrong thing, press Esc
  4. If the terminal seems stuck, press Ctrl+C
  5. If you were setting something up, use /workshop-queries
  6. If you are still stuck, raise your hand
